programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Bing agus a charaidean a’ tarraing dealbh do Gilly, tha Teàrlaidh a' cur sgròb mhòr air feadh an deilbh aige-san ach tha Gilly a sealltainn dhaibh nach b' e droch rud a bh’ ann. When Bing and his friends draw a picture for Gilly, Charlie does a squiggle on Bing’s picture. But Gilly shows them that this is not such a bad thing.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Bing aig taigh Sula ’son Pàrtaidh Aodach-oichdh’, tha e a' gabhail feagal nuair a tha e a' cluinntinn meanglan mòr, sgrìobach bho muigh. Ach, an uairsin, tha e ag ionnsachadh nach eil rudan eagallach cho eagallach sa shaoileas tu. When Bing is at Sula’s house for a PJ Party, he gets frightened when he hears a large scratchy branch outside. At the end of the day though, he learns that things aren’t as scary as you think they are.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha Hari air mìlsean bhlasta a bhèiceadh airson Ela agus Seren - cèic teòclaid! Bidh aon Abadas air a thaghadh airson a dhol a shealltainn airson rudeigin eile cruinn agus milis. Dè bhios ann? Hari has prepared a yummy treat for Ela and Seren - a chocolate cake! One Abadas will be chosen to go on another exciting adventure looking for something round and sweet-smelling. What could it be?

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: ’S e latha air leth fliuch a th’ ann, is tha Àtaidh a’ lorg toll ann am mullach an taighe. An uair sin tha e a’ mothachadh gu bheil tuill ann an tòrr rudan san taigh aige. Tha e a’ co-dhùnadh toll a chladhach dha fhèin, ach tha e a' steigeadh ann! Ciamar a gheibh Tilidh, Nìp agus na Boga-bogadaich às e? It is a very rainy day and Abney finds a hole in his roof. Then he starts to notice holes everywhere. He decides to dig one of his own but gets stuck in it! How will Teal, Neep and the Poc-Pocs get him out?

programme.title: ’S E Iasg a Th’Annam (I’m a Fish)
programme.desc: Tha an Tuna ag innse dhuinn cho luath ‘s a tha iad agus mar a tha iad fìor mhath gu sealg. Bidh iad a' sealg len caraidean - na leumadairean – oir bidh iadsan gan cumail sàbhailt’ o chearbain 's madaidhean-cuain acrach! The Tuna Fish tells us how speedy they are and how they are good predators. They hunt with their friends the dolphins - who keep them safe from threats like hungry sharks and killer whales.

programme.title: Orain CBeebies
programme.desc: Òrain mu bhith aig muir bho Carrie, Linda, Ruairidh agus sgioba CBeebies ALBA. A selection of seafaring songs from Carrie, Linda, Ruairidh and the CBeebies ALBA presenters.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Iain MacAonghais a’ leughadh Am Pàrtaidh Teatha aig Dadaidh Leòmhann. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Mike Sperring agus a dhealbhachadh le Sarah Warburton. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Mòrag Stiùbhart. A bedtime story for young children. Iain MacInnes reads Am Pàrtaidh Teatha aig Dadaidh by Mike Sperring, illustrated by Sarah Warburton and translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha Cuirm na Granndachd a’ gabhail àit’ far am faigh iad a mach cò as gràinnde de na Bògaisean. Ach cò an Gumbal a tha na Ghumbal nam Beachd? The Ugly Pageant is taking place where they decide on the ugliest Bògais. But which Gumbal is the Ideas-gumbal?

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Bonns a-muigh a’ lorg biadh airson na bangaid meadhan-oidhche, tha na Cnuimhean ga ghlacadh ’s ga chur am bruid. Ciamar a gheibh e air adhart an dèidh sin? When Bonns is out finding food for his 12-course midnight snack, the Cnuimhean catch and kidnap him. How will he get on after that?

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha an tuathanach a' co-dhùnadh raon goilf a thogail air an tuathanas gus aire an sguibhir ionadail a ghlacadh. Nuair a mhothachas an treud gun caill iad an dump aca air a bheil iad cho dèidheil, feumaidh iad a thighinn an àrda le plana innleachdail gus a shàbhaladh. The farmer decides to build a golf course on the farm to impress the local squire. When the flock discover they'll lose their beloved dump, they must come up with an imaginative solution to try and save it.

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Tha rudeigin dìomhair mun nighean ùr a th’ air an t-sràid – agus dè an gnothach a th’ aice ri trom-laighe Dhaibhidh? Tha Hilda airson a chuideachadh gus am faigh e seachad air an eagal a th’ air aig àm cadail. There is something mysterious about the new girl on the street. And what does she have to do with Daibhidh’s nightmares? Hilda wants to help him get over his fear of night time.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: Tha na seòid a’ feuchainn rud a-mach às an àbhaist ‘s a’ dèanamh biadh bhèagan. The lads venture out of their comfort zone and go plant-based.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: The studio guest is Iain MacPherson who hails from Alberta, Canada, and Calum Maclean visits a thriving community project in Glasgow.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Port An Obain
programme.desc: In the village of Appin, Gregor MacCormick shows his collection of vintage engines, and retired sea captain Eric Smith visits the new lighthouse ship, the Pole Star. Ann a baile Appain tha Gregor MacCormaig a sealltainn na seann einseanean. Agus anns an Obain tha Captein Eric Mac’a Ghobhainn a ceilidh air am Pole Star ura. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Ro Thrath don t-Saoghal/Born too Soon
programme.desc: Tha Daisy a’ faighinn leigheas èiginneach agus i a’ strì ri a h-anail a tharraing, fhad ’s a tha Treasa agus Ian a’ cur fàilte air na leth-aoin aca agus gan ullachadh fhèin airson Joshua a chall. Tha piseach a’ tighinn air Diane, agus thèid Méabh a ghluasad nas fhaisge air a dachaigh. Daisy receives emergency treatment for severe breathing problems, while Treasa and Ian welcome their twins and prepare to lose Joshua. Diane makes progress, and Méabh is transferred closer to home. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Is docha nach eil Zac cho òg is a bha e ach chan eil sin ag radh gum bu choir dha a sguir a bhruadar. Tha a chridhe a seinn , ach an can duine gur e ceòl a th'air a bhilean? Zac has never settled into normal, responsible adult life, and he wants one more chance at pop stardom. When opportunity knocks, he opens the door and grabs it with both hands, making sure no strings are left unpulled.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: Tha Bagelean Abigail fìor bhlast' agus sònraicht' 'son bruinse no lòn, no fiù 's aig àm sam bith, 's 'ad gad shàsachadh ann an dòigh nach gabh inns' 's iad fèìr taght' 'son an roinn leis an teaghlach no le caraidean. Abigail’s bagels are a very special and tasty brunch or lunch, or anytime experience, satisfying to the extreme and just the thing to share with family and friends. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Glan Fhèin
programme.desc: Angela clashes with angry locals shouting about short-term lets. Betty and Dido de-escalate things and share some home truths. There’s a sticky situation when an activist called Adam sneaks through the catflap with a tube of superglue. Meanwhile, Daniel tests Katie’s management methods by renegotiating his contract. And a corporate relaunch that is definitely not a party features costumes, cocktails, new clients and wild dance moves. Ultimately the rivals seem to be getting closer than ever.

programme.title: An t-Uisge/Rain Stories
programme.desc: Rain’s effect on our culture - including a frog wedding in India. Buaidh an uisge air ar cultar – a’ gabhail a-steach banais eadar dà losgann sna h-Innseachan.

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: Suidhichte taobh a-staigh Cearcall na h-Artaig, tha Eileanan Lofoten ann an Nirribhidh a’ tabhann luach fad-beatha de thoileachas don luchd-turais a bhitheas a’ tadhal ann. Air a tharraing leis an t-sreap agus an surfadh air leth a tha ri fhaotainn ann, tha Coinneach MacFhraing a’ siubhal timcheall nan eilean còmhla ri a chompanach, Calum Gibb, gus eòlas fhaighinn air an t-àite miorbhaileach seo. Situated within the Arctic Circle, Norway’s Lofoten islands offer a lifetime’s worth of exploration in the outdoors. Attracted by the world-class climbing and surfing on offer, Coinneach Rankin journeys around the islands with his companion, Calum Gibb, to glean unique experiences.

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Tha Sif, Pipp agus Bran a’ dol a chladhach airson ionmhais àrsaidh san t-sloc-gainmhich. Ziff, Pipp and Button set out to unearth ancient treasures buried in the garden sandpit.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Mossy air bhioran gus a charaid ùr, Fred, a thoirt gu cruinneachaidh-cluich an sgioba. Ge-tà ‘s e deargann a th’ ann am Fred ‘s chan eil càch cho toilichte a leithid fhaicinn nam measg... gus an seall Fred g’ eil e feumail na dhòigh fhèin! Mossy is excited to bring his new friend, Fred, to today’s playdate, but the rest of the gang are less than enamoured when they learn that Fred is actually a flea! However, Fred soon shows that he is quite useful to have around!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha bràmair aig Bernie ‘s tha i gus tighinn gu dìnnear a-nochd! Ge-tà, chan eil dad a dh'fhios aig Bernie dè chuireas e air dòigh! Tha Oona ‘s Baba ag aontachadh a chuideachadh ach, le Mossy nam meag, saoil am bi biadh air fhàgail mus nochd i? Bernie has a girlfriend – and she’s on her way to the grotto for dinner! However, Bernie has no idea what to prepare for her! Oona and Baba agree to help him out but, with Mossy joining the fray, will there be any food left for the special guest?

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Feumaidh an Dùd Beag a bhith far an urrainn dha bhith dùdach fad’ an là. Gu mì-fhortanach, chaidh e air seachran ach fhuair e a shlighe dhachaidh gu Planaid nan Dùd, le beagan taic bho a charaidean ùra Little Dùd needs to be where he can hoot all day. Unfortunately, he goes missing but finds his way back home to Planet Dùd, with a little help from his new friends.

programme.title: Orain CBeebies
programme.desc: Òrain mu bhith aig muir bho Carrie, Linda, Ruairidh agus sgioba CBeebies ALBA. A selection of seafaring songs from Carrie, Linda, Ruairidh and the CBeebies ALBA presenters.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Angela NicAoidh a’ leughadh Ugh na Cailleach-oidhche Bheag. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Debi Gliori agus a dhealbhachadh le Alison Brown. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Angela Mackay reads Ugh na Cailleach-oidhche Bheag by Debi Gliori, illustrated by Alison Brown and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: SpongeBob
programme.desc: Tha Mgr. Crùbag a’ cur Laraidh os cionn an taigh-bìdh rè ùine. Mr Krabs makes Larry the Lobster temporary manager.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Latha eile aig Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche agus tha Mrs NicArtair air tàlant ùr a lorg sa chlas ealain aice. Chan eil an Tidsear Stiùiridh, Mgr Hobson, cinnteach gur e tàlant a th’ air cùlaibh na h-ealaine ach ma dh'fhaoidte trioblaid! Aig an aon àm, tha Mgr Mackle a’ dèanamh oidhirp a bhith nas fhallaine. Mrs MacArthur has unearthed a new talent in her art class. Mr Hobson is not so sure if it is talent or perhaps a more troubling issue that’s behind the artwork. Meanwhile, Mr Mackle is busy with a new health kick.

programme.title: Alba Eagalach
programme.desc: Tha sgioba CBBC ALBA a’ toirt thugainn cuid de na sgeulachdan agus na tachartasan as eagalaiche ann an eachdraidh na h-Alba. Anns a’ phrògram seo, gheibh sinn a-mach mu chuid de na nithean neònach os-nàdarrach a tha tric a’ nochdadh ann am beul-aithris le teintean-biorach, caointichean agus tàcharain nam measg. The CBBC ALBA team brings us some of the scariest stories in Scottish history. In this episode, we delve into the paranormal with some of the strangest phenomena in Scottish folklore, including the will-o'-the-wisp, wailing women and changelings.

programme.title: Geamaichean Gorach
programme.desc: Tha Olaidh agus Coinneach ann an Ruisia agus chan e dìreach sgìtheadh a tha a’ gabhail àite oir tha sinn a’ faicinn tanca, saighdearan a’ caismeachd agus…. geama leigeil-shaighdear? Olaidh and Coinneach are in Russia but skiing isn’t the only thing that’s going on - there’s a tank to be seen, soldiers marching and....a game of skittles?

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Tha Sebastian a' cur crìoch air an stòraidh, - ag innse mar a dh'fhàs e fhèin is Belle dlùth, an dèidh dha a dìon bho mhuinntir a' bhaile. Sebastian tells the second part of the story, revealing how he and Belle got close, as a result of him protecting her from the people of the village.

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Le beathaichean Tuathanas Mossybottom a' coimhead geama ping pong eadar Seonaidh agus Bitzer, chan eil iad a' mothachadh gu bheil sionnach acrach a' dabhdail timcheall. With the animals of Mossybottom Farm keenly watching Shaun v Bitzer in the greatest table tennis match of all time, they fail to notice a hungry fox who isn't keeping his eye on the ball at all.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: Tha trèat sònraicht' aig Abigail, trèat ùr agus blasta de Fhritearan Mearag-bheag agus Peasair. Fèir ceart 'son a bhith air bòrd lòin air no bòrd bruinse, nuair a tha an teaghlach no caraidean ri tadhal. Abigail has a special treat in store in the form of fresh and tasty courgette and pea fritters. It's perfect for adding to that table top brunch or lunch spread when family or friends are visiting. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Fonn mo Bheatha
programme.desc: Taghadh den ceòl is òrain bhon seinneadairean 's luchd-ciùil a bha an sàs san t-sreath. A selection of music and song from the series.

programme.title: Bus Ghlaschu/Glasgow Bus
programme.desc: Thig còmhla ri Packie Bonner, an seann glèidheadair aig Celtic, air ais air Bus Ghlaschu. Follow ex-Celtic goalkeeper Packie Bonner as he relives his journeys on the Glasgow bus.

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Farpais-cheist do-chreidsinneach... Mas Fhìor! Le ochdnar Mas Fhìoraich a’ cluich bhon dachaighean fhèin, ’s iad an fheadhainn a chuireas na ceistean agus na freagairtean. An urrainn do Kerrie is Ceitidh agus Beniamin is Calum a tha a’ cluich bhon stiùideo, a’ chùis a dhèanamh orra airson an duais mhòr a bhuannachadh? A quiz show that is pretty unbelievable! Eight pretenders play from the comfort of their own homes and hold all the questions and answers to this quiz. Can Kerry and Katie, with Benjamin and Calum in the studio, beat the Pretenders for a chance to win a cash prize? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Tannadice '87
programme.desc: Tha 2017 a' comharrachadh an 30mh ceann-bliadhna bho rinn Dundee United FC rud a bha mòran dhaoine a' smaointinn a bha do-dheànta dhaibh: faighinn gu cuairt dheireannach Cupa UEFA. Tha Tannadice87 ag innse sgeulachd iongantach an iomairt Eòrpaich sin, bliadhna san do theab Dundè, a tha ainmeil airson silidh, diut agus naidheachdas, clach eile a chur air càrn urraim a' bhaile. 2017 marks the 30th anniversary of the year that Dundee United FC delivered on what many believed to be an impossible goal; reaching the final of the UEFA Cup. Tannadice '87 tells the remarkable story of this European adventure, a year in which dreams became reality, and Dundee, a city with a reputation for jam, jute and journalism added a fourth 'j' to its trademark: jubilation.

programme.title: An Cruinne Caochlaideach/Dynamic Planet
programme.desc: As the ice drastically melts, we see how science, nature and tradition can prepare us for the future.

programme.title: Faodail: Beatha nan Eilean (Shorts)
programme.desc: Archive film of communities from the 1930s to the 1980s, illustrating a time of many changes in the way of life on the Outer Hebrides. The strong community ties of past generations still influence the islands today. Filmichean bho Thasglann Faodail | Found Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 1980an, a’ clàradh dhòighean-beatha ag atharrachadh sna h-eileanan, a’ sgrùdadh beatha teaghlaich. Tha ceanglaichean coimhearsnachd làidir nan ginealaichean a dh’fhalbh fhathast a’ toirt buaidh air na h-eileanan an-diugh. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Prògram de cheòl traidiseanta agus freumhach air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. Air fhilmeadh aig àm Celtic Connections 2024 agus a’ taisbeanaidh chlàraidhean is chòmhraidhean a chaidh a dhèanamh a dh’aona ghothach airson Seirm, chìte cuid den luchd-ciùil a b’ fheàrr a bha aig an fhèis, leithid Carlene Carter, Eòghann MacEunraig, Talisk, Sarah Jarosz & Muireann Bradley. Traditional and roots music show presented by Mary Ann Kennedy. Filmed during Celtic Connections 2024, Seirm showcases bespoke recordings and conversations with some of the best artists appearing at the festival. This episode features performances from Carlene Carter, Ewen Henderson, Talisk and intimate session recordings with Sarah Jarosz and Muireann Bradley. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha Hari air mìlsean bhlasta a bhèiceadh airson Ela agus Seren - cèic teòclaid! Bidh aon Abadas air a thaghadh airson a dhol a shealltainn airson rudeigin eile cruinn agus milis. Dè bhios ann? Hari has prepared a yummy treat for Ela and Seren - a chocolate cake! One Abadas will be chosen to go on another exciting adventure looking for something round and sweet-smelling. What could it be?

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Bidh Latha na Cloinne ann a dh’aithghearr agus tha Peicein is a charaidean a’ cur romhpa tuairmsean a thoirt dham pàrantan a thaobh na preusantan a tha iad ag iarraidh. Ged nach eil iad a’ faighinn na bha iad ag iarraidh, tha iad ag iomlaid nam preusantan aca le chèile, is aig deireadh an latha tha iad a’ faighinn na bha iad ag iarraidh. Children’s Day is approaching, so Petit and his friends decide to give their parents clues on what gifts they want. Even though the youngsters don't receive their exact wishes, they end up exchanging presents to get what they all wanted.

programme.title: Pompon Am Mathan Beag/Pompon Little Bear
programme.desc: Gus nach tachair an aon rud a-màireach, ithidh Pompon biadh “glan” gus nach bi aige ri fhiaclan a ghlanadh. Ach a' cheist mhòr: a bheil a leithid a rud ann ri biadh glan? Pompon missed the sun rising as he had to clean his teeth. To avoid the same happening tomorrow, Pompon decides to eat 'clean' food so as to avoid brushing his teeth. But is there such a thing as 'clean' food?

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: ’S e latha air leth fliuch a th’ ann, is tha Àtaidh a’ lorg toll ann am mullach an taighe. An uair sin tha e a’ mothachadh gu bheil tuill ann an tòrr rudan san taigh aige. Tha e a’ co-dhùnadh toll a chladhach dha fhèin, ach tha e a' steigeadh ann! Ciamar a gheibh Tilidh, Nìp agus na Boga-bogadaich às e? It is a very rainy day and Abney finds a hole in his roof. Then he starts to notice holes everywhere. He decides to dig one of his own but gets stuck in it! How will Teal, Neep and the Poc-Pocs get him out?

programme.title: Sionnach agus Maigheach (Fox & Hare)
programme.desc: Tha Maigheach, Sionnach, Comhachag agus Tosg a’ faighinn cuireadh gu geama croquet còmhla ri Feòrag. Cò tha a’ nochdadh gun fhiathachadh ach Seoc! Chan eil diù aige do riaghailtean agus tha e a’ milleadh a’ ghnothaich air càch. Dìreach mus fheum iad uile sguir a chluich tha Maigheach a’ cur car anns na riaghailtean agus a’ toirt a chreidsinn air Seoc gu bheil e ri cealgaireachd an uair a tha e ann an dha-rìribh a’ cluich a’ gheama dìreach mar bu chòir. Brush invites Hare, Fox, Owl and Tusk for a fancy game of croquet. Jack shows up uninvited and wants to play, too. But being a villain, he can’t stand rules and ruins the game for everyone. Just at the moment the friends are about to give up, Hare reverses the rules to make Jack think he’s cheating but in fact he’s playing the game perfectly.

programme.title: SpongeBob
programme.desc: Tha Mgr. Crùbag a’ cur Laraidh os cionn an taigh-bìdh rè ùine. Mr Krabs makes Larry the Lobster temporary manager.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Latha eile aig Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche agus tha Mrs NicArtair air tàlant ùr a lorg sa chlas ealain aice. Chan eil an Tidsear Stiùiridh, Mgr Hobson, cinnteach gur e tàlant a th’ air cùlaibh na h-ealaine ach ma dh'fhaoidte trioblaid! Aig an aon àm, tha Mgr Mackle a’ dèanamh oidhirp a bhith nas fhallaine. Mrs MacArthur has unearthed a new talent in her art class. Mr Hobson is not so sure if it is talent or perhaps a more troubling issue that’s behind the artwork. Meanwhile, Mr Mackle is busy with a new health kick.

programme.title: Alba Eagalach
programme.desc: Tha sgioba CBBC ALBA a’ toirt thugainn cuid de na sgeulachdan agus na tachartasan as eagalaiche ann an eachdraidh na h-Alba. Anns a’ phrògram seo, gheibh sinn a-mach mu chuid de na nithean neònach os-nàdarrach a tha tric a’ nochdadh ann am beul-aithris le teintean-biorach, caointichean agus tàcharain nam measg. The CBBC ALBA team brings us some of the scariest stories in Scottish history. In this episode, we delve into the paranormal with some of the strangest phenomena in Scottish folklore, including the will-o'-the-wisp, wailing women and changelings.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Nuair tha taisbeanadh sgoile ri obrachadh air thairis air na saor-laithean – mu bheathaichean sgìreil, tron gheamhradh – tha Camshron ‘son na comharran às àird’ sa chlas fhaighinn, agus, mar as àbhaist, tha e ri foill! When there’s a school presentation to work on in the holidays, about regional animals during winter, Cameron wants the highest marks in the class and, as usual, he cheats!

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Faodail: Beatha nan Eilean (Shorts)
programme.desc: Footage from the Faodail | Found Film Archive of the Outer Hebrides from the 1930s to the 1980s, charting growing up in the islands. The strong community ties of past generations still influence the islands today. Filmichean bho Thasglann Faodail | Found Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 1980an, a’ clàradh mar a bhathar a’ fàs suas sna h-eileanan. Tha ceanglaichean coimhearsnachd làidir nan ginealaichean a dh’fhalbh fhathast a’ toirt buaidh air na h-eileanan an-diugh. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Somhairle Spins
programme.desc: Tha slighe dùbhlanach aig Somhairle agus a bhràthair Innes air a’ chiad latha aca a’ rothaireachd eadar Inbhir Nis agus Glaschu air an Badger Divide. Somhairle and his brother Innes have a challenging start on their first day cycling between Inverness and Glasgow on the Badger Divide.

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc: Skipinnish le Alive ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann. Skipinnish perform Alive in front of thousands of fans at a concert celebrating 25 years of the band, from Edinburgh Castle.

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Farpais-cheist do-chreidsinneach... Mas Fhìor! Le ochdnar Mas Fhìoraich a’ cluich bhon dachaighean fhèin, ’s iad an fheadhainn a chuireas na ceistean agus na freagairtean. An urrainn do Kerrie is Ceitidh agus Beniamin is Calum a tha a’ cluich bhon stiùideo, a’ chùis a dhèanamh orra airson an duais mhòr a bhuannachadh? A quiz show that is pretty unbelievable! Eight pretenders play from the comfort of their own homes and hold all the questions and answers to this quiz. Can Kerry and Katie, with Benjamin and Calum in the studio, beat the Pretenders for a chance to win a cash prize? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Orain Oir
programme.desc: Taghadh às na tasglainn - seinneadairean Gàidhlig tro na bliadhnaichean. Archive performances of Gaelic song, through the decades.

programme.title: Bus Ghlaschu/Glasgow Bus
programme.desc: Thig còmhla ri Packie Bonner, an seann glèidheadair aig Celtic, air ais air Bus Ghlaschu. Follow ex-Celtic goalkeeper Packie Bonner as he relives his journeys on the Glasgow bus.

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: Suidhichte taobh a-staigh Cearcall na h-Artaig, tha Eileanan Lofoten ann an Nirribhidh a’ tabhann luach fad-beatha de thoileachas don luchd-turais a bhitheas a’ tadhal ann. Air a tharraing leis an t-sreap agus an surfadh air leth a tha ri fhaotainn ann, tha Coinneach MacFhraing a’ siubhal timcheall nan eilean còmhla ri a chompanach, Calum Gibb, gus eòlas fhaighinn air an t-àite miorbhaileach seo. Situated within the Arctic Circle, Norway’s Lofoten islands offer a lifetime’s worth of exploration in the outdoors. Attracted by the world-class climbing and surfing on offer, Coinneach Rankin journeys around the islands with his companion, Calum Gibb, to glean unique experiences.

programme.title: Greim-Bìdh le Gregor
programme.desc: Gregor MacLeod takes fresh langoustines from a local fisherman to make paella, plus raspberry jam from an honesty box is used in a roly-poly.

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Prògram de cheòl traidiseanta agus freumhach air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. Air fhilmeadh aig àm Celtic Connections 2024 le clàraidhean is còmhraidhean a chaidh a dhèanamh a dh’aona ghothach airson Seirm, chìte cuid den luchd-ciùil a b’ fheàrr a bha aig an fhèis, leithid Genticorum, Pine Tree Flyers, Kathryn Tickell & The Darkening, Tim O’Brien & Jan Fabricius is Ceitidh Nicphàrlain. Traditional and roots music show presented by Mary Ann Kennedy. Filmed during Celtic Connections 2024, Seirm showcases bespoke recordings and conversations with some of the best artists appearing at the festival. This episode features performances from Genticorum, Pine Tree Flyers, Kathryn Tickell & The Darkening, Tim O’Brien & Jan Fabricius and Katie Macfarlane. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Ro Thrath don t-Saoghal/Born too Soon
programme.desc: Tha Daisy a’ faighinn leigheas èiginneach agus i a’ strì ri a h-anail a tharraing, fhad ’s a tha Treasa agus Ian a’ cur fàilte air na leth-aoin aca agus gan ullachadh fhèin airson Joshua a chall. Tha piseach a’ tighinn air Diane, agus thèid Méabh a ghluasad nas fhaisge air a dachaigh. Daisy receives emergency treatment for severe breathing problems, while Treasa and Ian welcome their twins and prepare to lose Joshua. Diane makes progress, and Méabh is transferred closer to home. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Tha stèisean tele eadar-lìon Fraochy Bay a' toirt duais do dh'aona dhuine bochd is iad a' leasachadh an taigh aige, gun fhiosta dha. Ach de a bhios a' feitheamh air Walter McSwain nuair a thilleas e dhachaidh? Fraochy Bay WebTV are doing it themselves. But will the lucky recipient Walter McSwain feel at home when it's time for the big reveal?

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: Tha trèat sònraicht' aig Abigail, trèat ùr agus blasta de Fhritearan Mearag-bheag agus Peasair. Fèir ceart 'son a bhith air bòrd lòin air no bòrd bruinse, nuair a tha an teaghlach no caraidean ri tadhal. Abigail has a special treat in store in the form of fresh and tasty courgette and pea fritters. It's perfect for adding to that table top brunch or lunch spread when family or friends are visiting. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Tannadice '87
programme.desc: Tha 2017 a' comharrachadh an 30mh ceann-bliadhna bho rinn Dundee United FC rud a bha mòran dhaoine a' smaointinn a bha do-dheànta dhaibh: faighinn gu cuairt dheireannach Cupa UEFA. Tha Tannadice87 ag innse sgeulachd iongantach an iomairt Eòrpaich sin, bliadhna san do theab Dundè, a tha ainmeil airson silidh, diut agus naidheachdas, clach eile a chur air càrn urraim a' bhaile. 2017 marks the 30th anniversary of the year that Dundee United FC delivered on what many believed to be an impossible goal; reaching the final of the UEFA Cup. Tannadice '87 tells the remarkable story of this European adventure, a year in which dreams became reality, and Dundee, a city with a reputation for jam, jute and journalism added a fourth 'j' to its trademark: jubilation.

programme.desc: A short film introducing actor and Dickens authority Bransby Williams. From 1953.

programme.title: Scrooge with Bransby Williams
programme.desc: Bransby Williams plays the part of Scrooge in a reading of Charles Dickens's A Christmas Carol. First broadcast in 1952 and considered the BBC's first televised Dickens adaptation.

programme.title: Earth's Natural Wonders
programme.desc: A look at how, in many of the earth's natural wonders, animals can be a threat to the people who live there, or they can provide a means of survival.

programme.title: The Lost Neanderthals
programme.desc: The Mandrin Cave in southern France has been attracting the attention of archaeologists for 30 years. The cave was regularly occupied in prehistoric times, and a remarkable record of human habitation going back thousands of years has been preserved by its soils. In 2015, the remains of a Neanderthal were uncovered, and the archaeological evidence points to this individual, named Thorin, living in close proximity to newly arrived Homo sapiens. This documentary follows an international team of scientists as they discover and investigate precious relics of the Palaeolithic period, resulting in groundbreaking revelations about the human populations of around 50,000 years ago as researchers uncover some of the secrets of the Mandrin Cave.

programme.title: Yellowstone: Wildest Winter to Blazing Summer
programme.desc: Patrick follows the grizzly bears that are taking a risk with the weather by leaving their winter dens early. Hungry wolves are struggling to bring down their elk prey in the unusually shallow snow. And for great grey owls, it is the iciness of the snow that is hampering their hunts. Yellowstone's winter is always one of the most brutal on the planet. But 2016 saw weather records broken, and the wildlife was forced to adapt to survive. Kate Humble gets to grips with the science behind this remarkable season, from understanding the importance of the snowpack's structure as the melt begins to uncovering why Yellowstone's unique geology poses problems for some grazers' teeth.

programme.title: The Eagle Has Landed
programme.desc: All-action World War II adventure. On the morning of 6 November 1943, the military authorities in Berlin receive a simple message - 'The Eagle Has Landed'. In a daring kidnap attempt, a small force of crack German paratroopers are poised to snatch Winston Churchill and return with him to Germany. If they succeed in their mission, it could alter the course of the war. Who can stop them?

programme.title: Scene by Scene
programme.desc: Mark Cousins meets US director David Lynch, creator of such idiosyncratic and groundbreaking screen landmarks as Eraserhead, Blue Velvet and Twin Peaks.

programme.title: Blue Velvet
programme.desc: When the discovery of a severed ear in a field leads a small-town college student to a bewitching nightclub singer, he finds himself lost in a dark underworld of fear and depravity. A disturbing, unique exploration of the dark side of American suburbia from director David Lynch.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: From the magical films of the silent era to the celebrated work of director David Lean and high definition television, this documentary revisits films and interviews from the archive to answer the question of why Dickens's novels have inspired so many hundreds of adaptations on screen. This co-production with Dickens 2012 not only encapsulates the history of Dickens's time, but also of the 100 years in which his work has survived most acutely on screen. It is not only the stories, themes and characters of Dickens's writing that translate so well onto screen - Sergei Eisenstein argued that there is something essentially filmic in his unique prose style; that Dickens's rapid 'cutting' within scenes and from scene to scene coupled with his seamless mixture of the bizarrely comic with the terrifyingly profound was itself proto-cinematic. Dickens wrote the way a camera saw before film had been invented, and he remains to this day the most cinematic of writers.

programme.title: Earth's Natural Wonders
programme.desc: A look at how people push themselves to the limit to survive in some natural wonders. We visit Brazil, Ethiopia, Laos, the Faroe Islands and the Swiss Alps.

programme.desc: Patrick follows the grizzly bears that are taking a risk with the weather by leaving their winter dens early. Yellowstone's winter is always one of the most brutal on the planet. But 2016 saw weather records broken, and the wildlife was forced to adapt to survive. Kate Humble gets to grips with the science behind this remarkable season, from understanding the importance of the snowpack's structure as the melt begins to uncovering why Yellowstone's unique geology poses problems for some grazers' teeth.

A chronological celebration of country queens at the BBC, whether on Top of the Pops, OGWT, Later with Jools Holland, Parkinson or their own entertainment specials.

programme.title: Country Kings at the BBC

This 50 years-plus compilation is a chronological look at country kings as featured on BBC studio shows as varied as In Concert, Wogan, The Late Show and Later with Jools Holland, plus early variety shows presented by the likes of Lulu, Harry Secombe and Shirley Abicair.

programme.desc: Live coverage from day 1 of the 2026 UK Snooker Championship.

programme.title: The Crucible: 40 Golden Snooker Years
programme.desc: Steve Davis goes back to the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield to celebrate 40 years of the World Snooker Championship. If the walls of this famous regional theatre could talk, they would tell tales of tears, triumphs, occasional debauchery, laughter and top-class sport. With contributions from snooker legends Dennis Taylor, Stephen Hendry, Jimmy White and super-fans Stephen Fry and Richard Osman.

programme.title: Davis v Taylor: The '85 Black Ball Final
programme.desc: A look back at one of British sport's golden moments - the 1985 World Championship Snooker final. At its peak, over 18 and a half million people sat glued to their sets as Steve Davis and Dennis Taylor battled past midnight to a final and deciding black ball, BBC Two's biggest ever audience. Colin Murray journeys around the UK filling in the gaps on the first time that he was allowed to see the other side of midnight. Along the way he finds answers to questions such as where did Dennis's 'upside-down glasses' actually come from? What really went on behind those dressing room doors? How did you spread the news in a world without mobile phones? And how different would the lives of the two protagonists have been if the result had been reversed that night? Featuring contributions from Barry McGuigan, Ted Lowe, Stephen Hendry and Barry Hearn.

Yellowstone's winter is always one of the most brutal on the planet. But 2016 saw weather records broken, and the wildlife was forced to adapt to survive. Kate Humble gets to grips with the science behind this remarkable season, from understanding the importance of the snowpack's structure as the melt begins to uncovering why Yellowstone's unique geology poses problems for some grazers' teeth.

programme.title: The Crucible: 40 Golden Snooker Years
programme.desc: Steve Davis goes back to the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield to celebrate 40 years of the World Snooker Championship. If the walls of this famous regional theatre could talk, they would tell tales of tears, triumphs, occasional debauchery, laughter and top-class sport. With contributions from snooker legends Dennis Taylor, Stephen Hendry, Jimmy White and super-fans Stephen Fry and Richard Osman.

programme.title: Davis v Taylor: The '85 Black Ball Final
programme.desc: A look back at one of British sport's golden moments - the 1985 World Championship Snooker final. At its peak, over 18 and a half million people sat glued to their sets as Steve Davis and Dennis Taylor battled past midnight to a final and deciding black ball, BBC Two's biggest ever audience. Colin Murray journeys around the UK filling in the gaps on the first time that he was allowed to see the other side of midnight. Along the way he finds answers to questions such as where did Dennis's 'upside-down glasses' actually come from? What really went on behind those dressing room doors? How did you spread the news in a world without mobile phones? And how different would the lives of the two protagonists have been if the result had been reversed that night? Featuring contributions from Barry McGuigan, Ted Lowe, Stephen Hendry and Barry Hearn.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Cambridgeshire, the East Anglian air ambulance races to save farmer Jonathan Willis after a freak accident leaves him impaled on his forklift. When the crew arrive, they realise one wrong move could prove fatal. The rescue is complex and high risk, with medics battling to stabilise Jonathan in the middle of his own yard, before rushing him to a specialist major trauma unit. Featuring dramatic CCTV footage of the incident and first-hand accounts from Jonathan, his wife Wendy and paramedic Andy Bates, this is an extraordinary story of split-second decisions and sheer determination in the fight to save a life. Meanwhile, in the Scottish Highlands, farmers face devastating attacks on their lambs by white-tailed eagles, threatening livelihoods and sparking debate over how to protect flocks. And in Cheshire, reporter Paul Colgan joins police tackling the surge in illegal fly-tipping, exposing how organised gangs are blighting farmland across the region.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Bargain Hunt pitches up at the Detling Showground in Kent. Stephanie Connell is with the reds, who face a military challenge, while John Cameron and the blues hunt for an item with a connection to music or drama. The rivalry leads to plenty of friendly competition around the fair and dishes up some drama at the auction! Charlie Ross visits nearby Lullingstone Castle, former site of the UK’s first silk farm, and learns about some unusual former residents.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Amanda Holden is stepping into the fight against fraud – and this time, it’s personal. After scammers used her name and image to con victims out of thousands, Amanda is teaming up with Scam Interceptors to turn the tables. In this special episode, airing as part of BBC Scam Safe week, Amanda joins Rav Wilding and the team to expose the global web of criminals targeting UK victims, including those pretending to be her. Using the same remote access tech scammers rely on, the team will hack the hackers to monitor their operations in real time, before confronting the fraudsters and stopping scams before they happen.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: When Phil returns home to find someone hanging around his house, he decides to confront him and finds some incriminating evidence on his doorbell footage. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan takes a trip to a garden centre to highlight simple tips that can deter wannabe burglars. And Janet turns doorbell detective to foil an elaborate scam when she receives a brand new mobile phone.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Alistair Appleton helps a couple who have never lived in an older home but who are now ready to fall for a bit of period charm in either Norfolk or Suffolk. With a £270,000 budget and three lively whippets to please, they are after a dog-friendly garden and a slice of East Anglian architectural history to call home. Alistair also meets a willow farmer and discovers how this wonderfully sustainable crop is being woven into the future.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team help a charity get their iconic bus back on the road, Mark Stuckey reaches for the stars, fixing an unusual projector, and Will is wowed by the lost art of encaustic tiles.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants - Tess, Stuart, Eileen, Mel and Dan - battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: As Nigella says, 'Part of the balance of life lies in understanding that different days require different types of eating'. So in this episode, Nigella shares her favourite menu to help get that balance in the kitchen. For the days when something light and luscious is needed, Nigella's salad of salmon, avocado, watercress and pumpkin seeds fits perfectly. For the occasions that call for something a bit different, there is Nigella's chicken shawarma with an array of spices, sauces and flatbreads. Inspired by a spit-roasted Lebanese kebab, Nigella's oven-roasted version is fun, tasty and prefect for feeding a crowd. There has to be chocolate in the balance and Nigella shares two of her latest treats - a glossy liquorice and blackcurrant chocolate cake and her chocolate chip cookie dough pots - freshly baked pots of gooey cookie dough served with a dollop of ice cream or creme fraiche.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Cambridgeshire, the East Anglian air ambulance races to save farmer Jonathan Willis after a freak accident leaves him impaled on his forklift. When the crew arrive, they realise one wrong move could prove fatal. The rescue is complex and high risk, with medics battling to stabilise Jonathan in the middle of his own yard, before rushing him to a specialist major trauma unit. Featuring dramatic CCTV footage of the incident and first-hand accounts from Jonathan, his wife Wendy and paramedic Andy Bates, this is an extraordinary story of split-second decisions and sheer determination in the fight to save a life. Meanwhile, in the Scottish Highlands, farmers face devastating attacks on their lambs by white-tailed eagles, threatening livelihoods and sparking debate over how to protect flocks. And in Cheshire, reporter Paul Colgan joins police tackling the surge in illegal fly-tipping, exposing how organised gangs are blighting farmland across the region.

Meanwhile, reporter Paul Colgan is in Northern Ireland to meet volunteers behind Operation Brockwatch – a groundbreaking scheme using hidden cameras to protect badgers from ruthless illegal hunters.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Antiques meet archaeology in this episode from West Sussex. In the village of Fishbourne, Natasha Raskin Sharp learns about the discovery of a huge Roman palace by workmen in the 1960s. In the company of curator Dr Rob Symmons, she hears how part of the palace and its treasures were unearthed over eight summers by hundreds of volunteers. One of the highlights is an exquisite mosaic featuring mythical sea creatures around which the owner – a high-ranking Roman – and his guests would have sat to eat meals. Another highlight is a partially smashed statue of Emperor Nero and a remarkably rare rabbit bone. Hoping to unearth their own treasures are two teams of bargain hunters at Ardingly antiques fair. In blue are cousins Michelle and Emma, and in red are golfing pals Linda and Yvonne. With expert Caroline Hawley by their side, the reds get off to an explosive start, eyeing up a pair of powder flasks. Meanwhile, Emma spots a West German pottery vase, but expert Thomas Forrester doubts that profits will bloom at auction. Wielding his gavel at the auction is Nick Hall; can the experts’ bonus buys bring home the big bucks?

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: As Nigella says, 'Part of the balance of life lies in understanding that different days require different types of eating'. So in this episode, Nigella shares her favourite menu to help get that balance in the kitchen. For the days when something light and luscious is needed, Nigella's salad of salmon, avocado, watercress and pumpkin seeds fits perfectly. For the occasions that call for something a bit different, there is Nigella's chicken shawarma with an array of spices, sauces and flatbreads. Inspired by a spit-roasted Lebanese kebab, Nigella's oven-roasted version is fun, tasty and prefect for feeding a crowd. There has to be chocolate in the balance and Nigella shares two of her latest treats - a glossy liquorice and blackcurrant chocolate cake and her chocolate chip cookie dough pots - freshly baked pots of gooey cookie dough served with a dollop of ice cream or creme fraiche.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Cambridgeshire, the East Anglian air ambulance races to save farmer Jonathan Willis after a freak accident leaves him impaled on his forklift. When the crew arrive, they realise one wrong move could prove fatal. The rescue is complex and high risk, with medics battling to stabilise Jonathan in the middle of his own yard, before rushing him to a specialist major trauma unit. Featuring dramatic CCTV footage of the incident and first-hand accounts from Jonathan, his wife Wendy and paramedic Andy Bates, this is an extraordinary story of split-second decisions and sheer determination in the fight to save a life. Meanwhile, in the Scottish Highlands, farmers face devastating attacks on their lambs by white-tailed eagles, threatening livelihoods and sparking debate over how to protect flocks. And in Cheshire, reporter Paul Colgan joins police tackling the surge in illegal fly-tipping, exposing how organised gangs are blighting farmland across the region.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Antiques meet archaeology in this episode from West Sussex. In the village of Fishbourne, Natasha Raskin Sharp learns about the discovery of a huge Roman palace by workmen in the 1960s. In the company of curator Dr Rob Symmons, she hears how part of the palace and its treasures were unearthed over eight summers by hundreds of volunteers. One of the highlights is an exquisite mosaic featuring mythical sea creatures around which the owner – a high-ranking Roman – and his guests would have sat to eat meals. Another highlight is a partially smashed statue of Emperor Nero and a remarkably rare rabbit bone. Hoping to unearth their own treasures are two teams of bargain hunters at Ardingly antiques fair. In blue are cousins Michelle and Emma, and in red are golfing pals Linda and Yvonne. With expert Caroline Hawley by their side, the reds get off to an explosive start, eyeing up a pair of powder flasks. Meanwhile, Emma spots a West German pottery vase, but expert Thomas Forrester doubts that profits will bloom at auction. Wielding his gavel at the auction is Nick Hall; can the experts’ bonus buys bring home the big bucks?

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: As Nigella says, 'Part of the balance of life lies in understanding that different days require different types of eating'. So in this episode, Nigella shares her favourite menu to help get that balance in the kitchen. For the days when something light and luscious is needed, Nigella's salad of salmon, avocado, watercress and pumpkin seeds fits perfectly. For the occasions that call for something a bit different, there is Nigella's chicken shawarma with an array of spices, sauces and flatbreads. Inspired by a spit-roasted Lebanese kebab, Nigella's oven-roasted version is fun, tasty and prefect for feeding a crowd. There has to be chocolate in the balance and Nigella shares two of her latest treats - a glossy liquorice and blackcurrant chocolate cake and her chocolate chip cookie dough pots - freshly baked pots of gooey cookie dough served with a dollop of ice cream or creme fraiche.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.desc: In Cambridgeshire, the East Anglian air ambulance races to save farmer Jonathan Willis after a freak accident leaves him impaled on his forklift. When the crew arrive, they realise one wrong move could prove fatal. The rescue is complex and high risk, with medics battling to stabilise Jonathan in the middle of his own yard, before rushing him to a specialist major trauma unit. Featuring dramatic CCTV footage of the incident and first-hand accounts from Jonathan, his wife Wendy and paramedic Andy Bates, this is an extraordinary story of split-second decisions and sheer determination in the fight to save a life. Meanwhile, in the Scottish Highlands, farmers face devastating attacks on their lambs by white-tailed eagles, threatening livelihoods and sparking debate over how to protect flocks. And in Cheshire, reporter Paul Colgan joins police tackling the surge in illegal fly-tipping, exposing how organised gangs are blighting farmland across the region.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Bedfordshire, a scorching summer’s day turns to chaos when flames rip through the countryside. Farmers and firefighters join forces in a desperate battle to contain a fast-moving field fire threatening homes and livelihoods. With dramatic footage filmed by farmer and YouTuber George Saunders, we hear first-hand from those who faced the blaze – including the crews who risked everything to stop it from spreading. In Leicestershire, a beloved horse is in danger after plunging into a freezing swimming pool. As panic rises, a specialist fire and rescue team race to save it, with the help of a local farmer, before it’s too late. Meanwhile, reporter Paul Colgan is in Northern Ireland to meet volunteers behind Operation Brockwatch – a groundbreaking scheme using hidden cameras to protect badgers from ruthless illegal hunters.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A flat in Clapham, a terrace in Kent and a bungalow in Stoke-on-Trent are all sold under the hammer. Jacqui, Martin and Dion meet the successful bidders, including a mother and daughter taking on their first family development and a part-time property developer who spends more than five times his original budget.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Antiques meet archaeology in this episode from West Sussex. In the village of Fishbourne, Natasha Raskin Sharp learns about the discovery of a huge Roman palace by workmen in the 1960s. In the company of curator Dr Rob Symmons, she hears how part of the palace and its treasures were unearthed over eight summers by hundreds of volunteers. One of the highlights is an exquisite mosaic featuring mythical sea creatures around which the owner – a high-ranking Roman – and his guests would have sat to eat meals. Another highlight is a partially smashed statue of Emperor Nero and a remarkably rare rabbit bone. Hoping to unearth their own treasures are two teams of bargain hunters at Ardingly antiques fair. In blue are cousins Michelle and Emma, and in red are golfing pals Linda and Yvonne. With expert Caroline Hawley by their side, the reds get off to an explosive start, eyeing up a pair of powder flasks. Meanwhile, Emma spots a West German pottery vase, but expert Thomas Forrester doubts that profits will bloom at auction. Wielding his gavel at the auction is Nick Hall; can the experts’ bonus buys bring home the big bucks?

In Leicestershire, a beloved horse is in danger after plunging into a freezing swimming pool. As panic rises, a specialist fire and rescue team race to save it, with the help of a local farmer, before it’s too late. Meanwhile, reporter Paul Colgan is in Northern Ireland to meet volunteers behind Operation Brockwatch – a groundbreaking scheme using hidden cameras to protect badgers from ruthless illegal hunters.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Antiques meet archaeology in this episode from West Sussex. In the village of Fishbourne, Natasha Raskin Sharp learns about the discovery of a huge Roman palace by workmen in the 1960s. In the company of curator Dr Rob Symmons, she hears how part of the palace and its treasures were unearthed over eight summers by hundreds of volunteers. One of the highlights is an exquisite mosaic featuring mythical sea creatures around which the owner – a high-ranking Roman – and his guests would have sat to eat meals. Another highlight is a partially smashed statue of Emperor Nero and a remarkably rare rabbit bone. Hoping to unearth their own treasures are two teams of bargain hunters at Ardingly antiques fair. In blue are cousins Michelle and Emma, and in red are golfing pals Linda and Yvonne. With expert Caroline Hawley by their side, the reds get off to an explosive start, eyeing up a pair of powder flasks. Meanwhile, Emma spots a West German pottery vase, but expert Thomas Forrester doubts that profits will bloom at auction. Wielding his gavel at the auction is Nick Hall; can the experts’ bonus buys bring home the big bucks?

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Bedfordshire, a scorching summer’s day turns to chaos when flames rip through the countryside. Farmers and firefighters join forces in a desperate battle to contain a fast-moving field fire threatening homes and livelihoods. With dramatic footage filmed by farmer and YouTuber George Saunders, we hear first-hand from those who faced the blaze – including the crews who risked everything to stop it from spreading. In Leicestershire, a beloved horse is in danger after plunging into a freezing swimming pool. As panic rises, a specialist fire and rescue team race to save it, with the help of a local farmer, before it’s too late. Meanwhile, reporter Paul Colgan is in Northern Ireland to meet volunteers behind Operation Brockwatch – a groundbreaking scheme using hidden cameras to protect badgers from ruthless illegal hunters.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A flat in Clapham, a terrace in Kent and a bungalow in Stoke-on-Trent are all sold under the hammer. Jacqui, Martin and Dion meet the successful bidders, including a mother and daughter taking on their first family development and a part-time property developer who spends more than five times his original budget.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Antiques meet archaeology in this episode from West Sussex. In the village of Fishbourne, Natasha Raskin Sharp learns about the discovery of a huge Roman palace by workmen in the 1960s. In the company of curator Dr Rob Symmons, she hears how part of the palace and its treasures were unearthed over eight summers by hundreds of volunteers. One of the highlights is an exquisite mosaic featuring mythical sea creatures around which the owner – a high-ranking Roman – and his guests would have sat to eat meals. Another highlight is a partially smashed statue of Emperor Nero and a remarkably rare rabbit bone. Hoping to unearth their own treasures are two teams of bargain hunters at Ardingly antiques fair. In blue are cousins Michelle and Emma, and in red are golfing pals Linda and Yvonne. With expert Caroline Hawley by their side, the reds get off to an explosive start, eyeing up a pair of powder flasks. Meanwhile, Emma spots a West German pottery vase, but expert Thomas Forrester doubts that profits will bloom at auction. Wielding his gavel at the auction is Nick Hall; can the experts’ bonus buys bring home the big bucks?

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: As Nigella says, 'Part of the balance of life lies in understanding that different days require different types of eating'. So in this episode, Nigella shares her favourite menu to help get that balance in the kitchen. For the days when something light and luscious is needed, Nigella's salad of salmon, avocado, watercress and pumpkin seeds fits perfectly. For the occasions that call for something a bit different, there is Nigella's chicken shawarma with an array of spices, sauces and flatbreads. Inspired by a spit-roasted Lebanese kebab, Nigella's oven-roasted version is fun, tasty and prefect for feeding a crowd. There has to be chocolate in the balance and Nigella shares two of her latest treats - a glossy liquorice and blackcurrant chocolate cake and her chocolate chip cookie dough pots - freshly baked pots of gooey cookie dough served with a dollop of ice cream or creme fraiche.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Charlie Ross is in Shropshire, where experts Tim Weeks and Ben Cooper try to help the teams make big profits when they head to the auction in Malvern. Charlie takes a trip into Shrewsbury to learn about the history of some 15th-century merchants, the Shrewsbury Drapers, and how they made the town so prosperous.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Cambridgeshire, the East Anglian air ambulance races to save farmer Jonathan Willis after a freak accident leaves him impaled on his forklift. When the crew arrive, they realise one wrong move could prove fatal. The rescue is complex and high risk, with medics battling to stabilise Jonathan in the middle of his own yard, before rushing him to a specialist major trauma unit. Featuring dramatic CCTV footage of the incident and first-hand accounts from Jonathan, his wife Wendy and paramedic Andy Bates, this is an extraordinary story of split-second decisions and sheer determination in the fight to save a life. Meanwhile, in the Scottish Highlands, farmers face devastating attacks on their lambs by white-tailed eagles, threatening livelihoods and sparking debate over how to protect flocks. And in Cheshire, reporter Paul Colgan joins police tackling the surge in illegal fly-tipping, exposing how organised gangs are blighting farmland across the region.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Cambridgeshire, the East Anglian air ambulance races to save farmer Jonathan Willis after a freak accident leaves him impaled on his forklift. When the crew arrive, they realise one wrong move could prove fatal. The rescue is complex and high risk, with medics battling to stabilise Jonathan in the middle of his own yard, before rushing him to a specialist major trauma unit. Featuring dramatic CCTV footage of the incident and first-hand accounts from Jonathan, his wife Wendy and paramedic Andy Bates, this is an extraordinary story of split-second decisions and sheer determination in the fight to save a life. Meanwhile, in the Scottish Highlands, farmers face devastating attacks on their lambs by white-tailed eagles, threatening livelihoods and sparking debate over how to protect flocks. And in Cheshire, reporter Paul Colgan joins police tackling the surge in illegal fly-tipping, exposing how organised gangs are blighting farmland across the region.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Bedfordshire, a scorching summer’s day turns to chaos when flames rip through the countryside. Farmers and firefighters join forces in a desperate battle to contain a fast-moving field fire threatening homes and livelihoods. With dramatic footage filmed by farmer and YouTuber George Saunders, we hear first-hand from those who faced the blaze – including the crews who risked everything to stop it from spreading. In Leicestershire, a beloved horse is in danger after plunging into a freezing swimming pool. As panic rises, a specialist fire and rescue team race to save it, with the help of a local farmer, before it’s too late. Meanwhile, reporter Paul Colgan is in Northern Ireland to meet volunteers behind Operation Brockwatch – a groundbreaking scheme using hidden cameras to protect badgers from ruthless illegal hunters.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A flat in Clapham, a terrace in Kent and a bungalow in Stoke-on-Trent are all sold under the hammer. programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Antiques meet archaeology in this episode from West Sussex. In the village of Fishbourne, Natasha Raskin Sharp learns about the discovery of a huge Roman palace by workmen in the 1960s. In the company of curator Dr Rob Symmons, she hears how part of the palace and its treasures were unearthed over eight summers by hundreds of volunteers. One of the highlights is an exquisite mosaic featuring mythical sea creatures around which the owner – a high-ranking Roman – and his guests would have sat to eat meals. Another highlight is a partially smashed statue of Emperor Nero and a remarkably rare rabbit bone. Hoping to unearth their own treasures are two teams of bargain hunters at Ardingly antiques fair. In blue are cousins Michelle and Emma, and in red are golfing pals Linda and Yvonne. With expert Caroline Hawley by their side, the reds get off to an explosive start, eyeing up a pair of powder flasks. Meanwhile, Emma spots a West German pottery vase, but expert Thomas Forrester doubts that profits will bloom at auction. Wielding his gavel at the auction is Nick Hall; can the experts’ bonus buys bring home the big bucks?

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Bedfordshire, a scorching summer’s day turns to chaos when flames rip through the countryside. Farmers and firefighters join forces in a desperate battle to contain a fast-moving field fire threatening homes and livelihoods. With dramatic footage filmed by farmer and YouTuber George Saunders, we hear first-hand from those who faced the blaze – including the crews who risked everything to stop it from spreading. In Leicestershire, a beloved horse is in danger after plunging into a freezing swimming pool. As panic rises, a specialist fire and rescue team race to save it, with the help of a local farmer, before it’s too late. programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Antiques meet archaeology in this episode from West Sussex. In the village of Fishbourne, Natasha Raskin Sharp learns about the discovery of a huge Roman palace by workmen in the 1960s. In the company of curator Dr Rob Symmons, she hears how part of the palace and its treasures were unearthed over eight summers by hundreds of volunteers. One of the highlights is an exquisite mosaic featuring mythical sea creatures around which the owner – a high-ranking Roman – and his guests would have sat to eat meals. Another highlight is a partially smashed statue of Emperor Nero and a remarkably rare rabbit bone. Hoping to unearth their own treasures are two teams of bargain hunters at Ardingly antiques fair. In blue are cousins Michelle and Emma, and in red are golfing pals Linda and Yvonne. With expert Caroline Hawley by their side, the reds get off to an explosive start, eyeing up a pair of powder flasks. Meanwhile, Emma spots a West German pottery vase, but expert Thomas Forrester doubts that profits will bloom at auction. Wielding his gavel at the auction is Nick Hall; can the experts’ bonus buys bring home the big bucks?

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: As Nigella says, 'Part of the balance of life lies in understanding that different days require different types of eating'. So in this episode, Nigella shares her favourite menu to help get that balance in the kitchen. For the days when something light and luscious is needed, Nigella's salad of salmon, avocado, watercress and pumpkin seeds fits perfectly. For the occasions that call for something a bit different, there is Nigella's chicken shawarma with an array of spices, sauces and flatbreads. Inspired by a spit-roasted Lebanese kebab, Nigella's oven-roasted version is fun, tasty and prefect for feeding a crowd. programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Cambridgeshire, the East Anglian air ambulance races to save farmer Jonathan Willis after a freak accident leaves him impaled on his forklift. When the crew arrive, they realise one wrong move could prove fatal. The rescue is complex and high risk, with medics battling to stabilise Jonathan in the middle of his own yard, before rushing him to a specialist major trauma unit. Featuring dramatic CCTV footage of the incident and first-hand accounts from Jonathan, his wife Wendy and paramedic Andy Bates, this is an extraordinary story of split-second decisions and sheer determination in the fight to save a life. Meanwhile, in the Scottish Highlands, farmers face devastating attacks on their lambs by white-tailed eagles, threatening livelihoods and sparking debate over how to protect flocks. And in Cheshire, reporter Paul Colgan joins police tackling the surge in illegal fly-tipping, exposing how organised gangs are blighting farmland across the region.

programme.desc: Amanda Holden is stepping into the fight against fraud – and this time, it’s personal. After scammers used her name and image to con victims out of thousands, Amanda is teaming up with Scam Interceptors to turn the tables. In this special episode, airing as part of BBC Scam Safe week, Amanda joins Rav Wilding and the team to expose the global web of criminals targeting UK victims, including those pretending to be her. Using the same remote access tech scammers rely on, the team will hack the hackers to monitor their operations in real time, before confronting the fraudsters and stopping scams before they happen.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Bedfordshire, a scorching summer’s day turns to chaos when flames rip through the countryside. Farmers and firefighters join forces in a desperate battle to contain a fast-moving field fire threatening homes and livelihoods. With dramatic footage filmed by farmer and YouTuber George Saunders, we hear first-hand from those who faced the blaze – including the crews who risked everything to stop it from spreading. In Leicestershire, a beloved horse is in danger after plunging into a freezing swimming pool. As panic rises, a specialist fire and rescue team race to save it, with the help of a local farmer, before it’s too late. Meanwhile, reporter Paul Colgan is in Northern Ireland to meet volunteers behind Operation Brockwatch – a groundbreaking scheme using hidden cameras to protect badgers from ruthless illegal hunters.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A flat in Clapham, a terrace in Kent and a bungalow in Stoke-on-Trent are all sold under the hammer. Jacqui, Martin and Dion meet the successful bidders, including a mother and daughter taking on their first family development and a part-time property developer who spends more than five times his original budget.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Antiques meet archaeology in this episode from West Sussex. In the village of Fishbourne, Natasha Raskin Sharp learns about the discovery of a huge Roman palace by workmen in the 1960s. In the company of curator Dr Rob Symmons, she hears how part of the palace and its treasures were unearthed over eight summers by hundreds of volunteers. One of the highlights is an exquisite mosaic featuring mythical sea creatures around which the owner – a high-ranking Roman – and his guests would have sat to eat meals. Another highlight is a partially smashed statue of Emperor Nero and a remarkably rare rabbit bone. Hoping to unearth their own treasures are two teams of bargain hunters at Ardingly antiques fair. In blue are cousins Michelle and Emma, and in red are golfing pals Linda and Yvonne. With expert Caroline Hawley by their side, the reds get off to an explosive start, eyeing up a pair of powder flasks. Meanwhile, Emma spots a West German pottery vase, but expert Thomas Forrester doubts that profits will bloom at auction. Wielding his gavel at the auction is Nick Hall; can the experts’ bonus buys bring home the big bucks?

programme.desc: 1983. A young surfer leaves Dolphin Cove in pursuit of his dreams. Forty-three years later, his remains are found in the concrete by the ocean pool. So in this episode, Nigella shares her favourite menu to help get that balance in the kitchen. For the occasions that call for something a bit different, there is Nigella's chicken shawarma with an array of spices, sauces and flatbreads. Inspired by a spit-roasted Lebanese kebab, Nigella's oven-roasted version is fun, tasty and prefect for feeding a crowd. There has to be chocolate in the balance and Nigella shares two of her latest treats - a glossy liquorice and blackcurrant chocolate cake and her chocolate chip cookie dough pots - freshly baked pots of gooey cookie dough served with a dollop of ice cream or creme fraiche.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Bedfordshire, a scorching summer’s day turns to chaos when flames rip through the countryside. Farmers and firefighters join forces in a desperate battle to contain a fast-moving field fire threatening homes and livelihoods. With dramatic footage filmed by farmer and YouTuber George Saunders, we hear first-hand from those who faced the blaze – including the crews who risked everything to stop it from spreading. In Leicestershire, a beloved horse is in danger after plunging into a freezing swimming pool. programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Antiques meet archaeology in this episode from West Sussex. In the village of Fishbourne, Natasha Raskin Sharp learns about the discovery of a huge Roman palace by workmen in the 1960s. In the company of curator Dr Rob Symmons, she hears how part of the palace and its treasures were unearthed over eight summers by hundreds of volunteers. One of the highlights is an exquisite mosaic featuring mythical sea creatures around which the owner – a high-ranking Roman – and his guests would have sat to eat meals. Another highlight is a partially smashed statue of Emperor Nero and a remarkably rare rabbit bone. Hoping to unearth their own treasures are two teams of bargain hunters at Ardingly antiques fair. In blue are cousins Michelle and Emma, and in red are golfing pals Linda and Yvonne. With expert Caroline Hawley by their side, the reds get off to an explosive start, eyeing up a pair of powder flasks. Meanwhile, Emma spots a West German pottery vase, but expert Thomas Forrester doubts that profits will bloom at auction. Wielding his gavel at the auction is Nick Hall; can the experts’ bonus buys bring home the big bucks?

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: As Nigella says, 'Part of the balance of life lies in understanding that different days require different types of eating'. So in this episode, Nigella shares her favourite menu to help get that balance in the kitchen. For the days when something light and luscious is needed, Nigella's salad of salmon, avocado, watercress and pumpkin seeds fits perfectly. For the occasions that call for something a bit different, there is Nigella's chicken shawarma with an array of spices, sauces and flatbreads. Inspired by a spit-roasted Lebanese kebab, Nigella's oven-roasted version is fun, tasty and prefect for feeding a crowd. There has to be chocolate in the balance and Nigella shares two of her latest treats - a glossy liquorice and blackcurrant chocolate cake and her chocolate chip cookie dough pots - freshly baked pots of gooey cookie dough served with a dollop of ice cream or creme fraiche.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Charlie Ross is in Shropshire, where experts Tim Weeks and Ben Cooper try to help the teams make big profits when they head to the auction in Malvern. programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.
